messages:
raj: Heads-up — I ran a focused perf profile on the latest PP+TP checkpointing branch (enable-checkpointing=true). Seeing a surprising jump in all-reduce time and end-to-end step latencies. Posting raw summary and a few notes, can folks weigh in?

josh: Thanks — can you paste the profiler output and which topology (TPxPP) + batch shapes?

raj: Sure. Setup: 8 GPUs, TP=2, PP=4, batch_tokens=2048, sequence=1024. Model: 20B variant, kv-cache enabled. Checkpointing: per-layer activation checkpointing (recompute enabled).

raj: Profiler snippet:```
STEP  (median) : 168.3 ms
ALLREDUCE (median) : 47.9 ms  (+36.0 ms vs non-checkpoint)
RECOMPUTE (median) : 59.4 ms
COMPUTE (other kernels): 41.0 ms
KV_CACHE_APPLY: 6.8 ms
```

anya: Wow allreduce almost 48ms. On non-checkpoint branch what was allreduce?

raj: Non-checkpoint baseline: STEP 120 ms, ALLREDUCE 11.5 ms, RECOMPUTE 0 ms (ofc). So net increase in step ~48 ms.

mike: Likely cause: checkpointing increases the number of backward passes (recompute) which changes scheduling so that we no longer overlap some all-reduces with compute. So effective communication windows become hot spots.

carla: Agree. Also TP/PP mapping matters — recompute expands contiguous compute phases that line up poorly with our current ring schedule. Need to look at comm/compute overlap traces (timeline).

raj: Attached flame view (pasted below) — you can see back-to-back allreduces during recompute windows.

raj: ```timeline: GPU0: recompute->allreduce->recompute->allreduce
GPU1: recompute->wait->allreduce->recompute
...```

josh: Two immediate levers: 1) change checkpoint granularity (group layers so recompute phases align with cheaper allreduces), 2) try async/fused all-reduce (NCCL multi-stream) to overlap with recompute.

anya: Could we also change kernel selection for the recompute kernels? Smaller kernels sometimes give better overlap because they finish earlier and allow comm to start sooner. Is the runtime picking different kernels when checkpointing?

raj: Yes, we saw more fp16->int8 fused kernels swapped out because sequence length pattern changed. That affected per-op durations. I have diff traces showing kernel_id shifts after enabling checkpointing.

mike: Another thought: KV cache behavior. With prefix caching enabled, memory pressure changes kernel tiling and triggers different batching heuristics. That can increase number of NCCL calls (more small allreduces) which hurts latency. Any measurements on allreduce size distribution?

raj: Good call — hist of allreduce sizes: baseline is mostly 2MB chunks; checkpoint branch shows many ~128KB small reductions (lots more calls). So overhead amortization is worse.

carla: Small allreduces are our enemy. Options: 1) fuse small grads into larger buffers before allreduce, 2) adjust TP partitioning to make local aggregation larger, 3) reduce checkpoint frequency at the layer boundaries that cross TP shards.

josh: For (1) we can try group_allreduce_buffers in the runtime — we have a flag but it's currently off for checkpoint mode due to correctness worries around in-place recompute. We should revisit with stricter pre/post barriers.

anya: For overlap: can we schedule async allreduce on a dedicated stream and trigger it earlier while recompute continues on main stream? Need to ensure we don't break gradient ordering. Might need a light synchronization barrier at end.

mike: NVLink topology also matters. Did you run on contiguous PCI peers or mixed racks? If ring crosses a slower link the cost multiplies. Perf-bot, can you paste interconnect map for that run?

perf-bot: interconnect: NVLINK fully connected per-socket; cross-socket -> 12GB/s. Run placed TP shards across sockets 0/1 causing cross-socket traffic for some allreduces.

carla: So combined issues: more smaller allreduces + some crossing slower links + recompute changing overlap windows. Not surprising we saw 36ms bump.

raj: Proposed next experiments:
- enable group_allreduce_buffers=true on checkpoint branch and measure
- try coarse-grained checkpointing (every 2 layers) to reduce recompute call frequency
- test NCCL async stream (multi-stream) overlap + enforced ordering barrier
- run with TP shards colocated intra-socket to avoid cross-socket where possible

josh: I'll own group_allreduce_buffers test. Will add a micro-batch fuse pass before gradient allreduce. Any concerns about memory transient peaks?

anya: Watch out for peak memory — fusing increases temporary buffer size. But we might still be net positive vs baseline because checkpointing reduces peak activations. Add a safety cap guard.

mike: I'll run topology colocate and async allreduce experiment. If that reduces allreduce median below ~20ms we can justify enabling checkpointing by default for this model.

carla: Also add a kernel-selection trace hook in the profiler so we can see which kernels flip when checkpointing toggles. That'll help tune heuristics for recompute kernels.

raj: Great. Action items: josh -> group_allreduce_buffers PR; mike -> async-nccl + topology runs; carla -> kernel trace hook; raj -> rerun baselines with coarse checkpointing and post KV-cache size distribution.

josh: One more note: we should add a CI perf test that simulates checkpointing + TP/PP mix so we detect regressions early.

anya: Agreed. Add an alert if allreduce median jumps > 2x vs baseline in nightly perf. :rotating_light:

raj: Thanks all. Will drop profiles in the perf channel and link results once experiments finish. :rocket:
